To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the light-chain variable domains from two AL patients were cytotoxic to cardiomyocytes in vitro, and the soluble oligomeric light-chain species in cell culture correspond to those found in circulation in these AL patients.

(1) soluble immunoglobulin LCs from AL patients are toxic to cells and the toxicity is mediated by soluble oligomers; (2) the toxicity is mediated via activation of caspases and calpain proteases and is associated with mitochondrial dysfunction; and (3) the toxicity is not mediated by oxidative stress or by the activation of the unfolded protein response.

1) the soluble form of two well-characterize immunoglobulin light chain amyloidogenic proteins from cardiac light chain amyloidosis patients is toxic to cardiomyocyte cells, 2) this toxicity is mediated by the formation of soluble oligomeric intermediates, and 3) the species present in cell culture correspond to the species present at similar concentration in the circulation of these patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the toxic properties of light chains from AL patients.
the cellular toxicity of immunoglobulin light chain proteins, a hallmark of AL.
the characterization of the toxic species of light chains in AL, and with the elucidation of the mechanism of toxicity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
light-chain amyloid proteins are toxic to cardiocytes, and that these species found in circulation are the ones that mediate toxicity.
light chains from AL patients are toxic to cells, and that soluble species of these proteins, including monomers, dimers, and oligomers, contribute to their toxicity.
the soluble species found in circulation, and in cell culture, are the most toxic to the cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
soluble light-chain amyloid proteins are toxic to cells, and that the toxicity is not caused by a particular amino-acid sequence but rather by the presence of the amyloidogenic protein in a cell.
we have shown that the soluble forms of the light-chain variable domains of two AL proteins are toxic to cardiocytes and that the soluble species found in circulation are the most toxic.
the soluble form and species of the AL light-chain proteins are cytotoxic, and the toxicity is related to the presence of somatic mutations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the soluble form(s) of immunoglobulin light chain present in circulation are cytotoxic to cells.
light-chain amyloid proteins, which are secreted by the cells that secrete them, are toxic to cells, and that these toxic proteins may be the main culprit for the pathogenesis of AL.
soluble light-chain species can be toxic to cells and that these species are present in circulation in AL patients.
